races.name: Betfred 'Nifty 50' Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Wise And Wonderful
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's colt arrives in fine order after winning over this exact course-and-distance combination 15 days ago, his form figures of 4-2-1-0 showing progressive improvement; David Probert rides for a yard firing at 8/56 in a 14-day window and the return to 7f good-to-firm is a confirmed positive.
runners_data.comment: Wise And Wonderful won two starts back and was second three starts back, showing she can compete at this level, and she returns fit on 15 days' rest with distance and going experience in her favour; the unplaced run last time out is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Bincimbal
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's filly is the only natural front-runner in the field and Hector Crouch will enjoy a free rail with no pace rivals to worry about; her two runs have both come on similar going at 7f and she shaped with promise on debut before an encouraging third, making her a live each-way threat if she translates that form to a racecourse like Epsom.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last two starts and ranked last on our figures, Bincimbal faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a reasonable freshness of 34 days from stall two.

runners_data.name: Greek Symphony
runners_data.note: Five days since her last run is short enough to check, but Oliver Cole's two-year-old has shown consistent form — placing at 7f on good and winning at 7f on standard — and Ashley Lewis (3lb claim) adds appeal; she should sit handy in second or third and the good-to-firm surface at Epsom suits horses who travel prominently and quicken.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, but a winner two starts back, Greek Symphony brings strong recent form to this test, has run over today's trip and going, and her rating of 82 heads this five-runner field — five days between runs is the only minor query.

runners_data.name: Minster Boy
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's colt holds a modest record (0W1P from three starts) and his form has largely been over 5f; stepping up to 7f for the first time, his hold-up style means he needs a genuinely strong pace to get home, which this small field with a single front-runner is unlikely to provide — a significant concern.
runners_data.comment: Minster Boy shaped with promise when second two starts back and has run over today's trip and conditions, while his rating of 76 marks him as a genuine threat from stall five; the risk is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Sequel Star
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's lightly raced filly has only two runs to her name, both over 6f, so this 7f trip on turf at Epsom is a step into the unknown; Kieran Shoemark takes the ride and the yard is operating at 8/44 over 14 days, but without any similar-going wins or places and facing a trip extension, she is difficult to assess with confidence.
runners_data.comment: Sequel Star showed promise with a third last time out and has experience over today's trip and conditions, making her a genuine threat from stall one carrying 130 lb; the concern is she remains yet to win in recent starts.

races.paceDynamic: Bincimbal is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no other horse in this five-runner field genuinely wired to lead, she should stride into an uncontested pace from the stalls and control the tempo through Epsom's 7f on good-to-firm ground. Wise And Wonderful and Greek Symphony will press forward from prominent positions, sitting a length or two off the leader rather than challenging for the rail, which keeps the early fractions honest but not searingly fast. Minster Boy will be restrained toward the rear, with Sequel Star — lightly raced and whose two runs have both been at 6f — an unknown quantity in terms of how she travels in behind. The race shape overwhelmingly favours prominent racers who can track a sustainable gallop and quicken into the straight, giving Wise And Wonderful and Greek Symphony the ideal platform; genuine hold-up horses face a stiff ask if the pace is merely moderate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bincimbal Controls, Pressed Late
scenarios.trigger: If Bincimbal leads at a steady-to-fair clip and the race is decided by a sustained duel in the straight.
scenarios.body: Bincimbal dictates throughout and, having conserved enough energy under Hector Crouch, fights on gamely; the prominent pair Wise And Wonderful and Greek Symphony arrive on her heels but must quicken past a horse that has had it all her own way.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the early fractions are genuinely slow and Bincimbal is never headed, conserving enough to repel all challengers.
scenarios.body: A falsely moderate gallop leaves Bincimbal with a winning margin in hand as the closers cannot generate sufficient momentum in a 7f test on quick ground; prominent runners still place but lack the finishing burst to peg back a horse that has loafed in front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves stronger than expected and the front two cry enough inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Minster Boy, switched wide and angled for a run, benefits from a genuinely true gallop that stretches the field and leaves the leaders vulnerable; Sequel Star, stepping up in trip from 6f with untapped potential, could also pick up late ground on a fast surface.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If something disrupts the early order — a slow break for Bincimbal or interference — and the race becomes messy and tactical.
scenarios.body: Without the anchor of a genuine front-runner, horses race out of their comfort zones and the race becomes a sprint from two out; in that scenario the most physically mature and tactically adaptable runner wins, with Wise And Wonderful best equipped to handle an unpredictable shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Wise And Wonderful, who won here over 7f 15 days ago, can track Bincimbal smoothly from a prominent position — if he gets a clean passage he arrives at the finish in the best possible shape.

Monitor Bincimbal's early stride rate; if Hector Crouch goes overly conservative at the head of affairs, a slow early tempo could turn the race into a sprint and undermine hold-up horses Minster Boy and Sequel Star entirely.

Greek Symphony ran only five days ago — watch for any signs of residual fatigue as the field turns into the straight, as a quick turnaround can blunt a two-year-old's finishing kick even on a fast surface.

Minster Boy's step up from 5f–6f to 7f for the first time is the key unknown; if he handles the extra yardage and the pace is honest, he is the one most likely to be finishing fastest of all in the closing stages — note where he is at the two-furlong pole.

races.name: Betfred 'Bet Builder' EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tiora Time
runners_data.note: Consistent filly with a recent win at 7f on Good ground (form: 3-1-2) and Tom Clover's in-form yard (T14: 5/17), making her the most credible prominent tracker; 1 day since last run is worth noting but not alarming for a yard operating confidently.

runners_data.name: Desert Symphony
runners_data.note: Two poor recent efforts (9th, 8th) on similar going suggest the form level is well below her OR=120 ceiling; a genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield mapping due to field congestion, and Pat Cosgrave will face a compressed closing scenario with limited room to manoeuvre.

runners_data.name: Diplomata
runners_data.note: William Haggas filly who has shown mid-pack form (4th, 5th) without threatening on both a 6f and 7f track, suggesting the trip is fine but she needs a searching pace to get competitive — 21 days off is not a concern for the yard.

runners_data.name: Secret Flite
runners_data.note: Weakest recent efforts of the three hold-up types (9th and 5th), and although the 15-day turnaround is routine, the form suggests she needs something to go wrong elsewhere to factor; Ashley Lewis claims 3lb which mitigates weight slightly.

runners_data.name: Tansy Lane
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, Kieran Shoemark has the luxury of an uncontested lead over 7f on fast ground; consecutive defeats (7th, 6th) at shorter trip suggest the step back up to 7f may suit, and the James Owen yard is operating at 9/45 (T14) — not electric but ticking over.

races.paceDynamic: Tansy Lane is the sole confirmed front-runner in a five-runner field and should stride to the lead unchallenged from the outset, setting a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground over Epsom's 7f. With Tiora Time likely to press from a prominent position behind, the pace should be honest without becoming a sprint, giving Tansy Lane a controlled rhythm that could prove difficult to peg back late. The three hold-up types — Desert Symphony, Diplomata, and Secret Flite — will all hunt off a single leader, meaning they face a compressed traffic scenario with limited room to exploit any weakness in the front two. This race shape strongly favours the lead-to-prominent profile: a single uncontested pace-setter on fast ground at Epsom, where the straight favours those who can sustain momentum rather than produce a late burst off a slow tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tansy Lane Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Tansy Lane leads uncontested and Tiora Time settles behind without pressing hard, the front-runner dictates a comfortable gallop and the hold-up trio are left with too much ground to make up on fast going.
scenarios.body: Tansy Lane rolls along in front without burning early energy and the tight closing kick the hold-up horses need simply never materialises in time.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tiora Time Applies Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Tiora Time tracks Tansy Lane aggressively and forces a genuinely strong gallop, a more gruelling test opens up the race for those travelling smoothly in behind.
scenarios.body: A contested pace on fast ground would suit a horse with strong finishing mechanics, and Tiora Time's recent win at 7f Good represents credible form at this trip and going.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Trio Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace collapses or Tansy Lane falters dramatically in the final furlong, the three closers get a late opening.
scenarios.body: Diplomata and Secret Flite are genuine hold-up types who need a strong pace to close into, and William Haggas's filly carries enough class to capitalise if conditions turn in her favour at the death.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Desert Symphony Disrupts Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Desert Symphony, a natural hold-up type mapped to midfield due to field compression, is ridden more forwardly than expected and switches tactics, the race shape fragments.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability scenario reliant on Desert Symphony racing entirely out of role on going that has already produced two below-par finishes, making it a significant discount.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Tiora Time's rider Charles Bishop pushes forward to press Tansy Lane — if he does, the pace dynamic tightens sharply and changes the shape from controlled to genuinely contested.

Desert Symphony's redistribution from hold-up to midfield means Pat Cosgrave may need to make an early decision about positioning; if she is inconvenienced by traffic off the sole front-runner, her already-modest recent form becomes harder to overcome.

Tansy Lane's back-to-back defeats at 6f suggest stamina at 7f is an open question — if she ties up inside the final furlong after controlling the race, the hold-up trio could collide into a tight finish.

Fast ground confirmed for this race (Good to Firm per going report) — all five runners have similar-going experience, so no single filly gains a surface edge, but it does reinforce that closers will need a stronger-than-expected gallop to close late.

With only five runners and three genuine hold-up types, watch for crowding on the home turn — if Diplomata and Secret Flite become blocked behind the same gaps, neither may get a clear run at the critical moment.

races.name: Betfred 'The Classic Bookmaker' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ruby's Profit
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner off 62 days' absence wearing headgear (tongue-tie), with patchy recent form including a 14th; Tom Ward's yard is quiet at 1/10 in 14 days and this trip is a furlong beyond her recent 5f runs, raising stamina questions in a contested pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Rated the pick of the field on our figures, Ruby's Profit has shown a couple of fourth places among otherwise modest recent efforts and has experience of today's trip and conditions, though she heads here winless in her last five and a 62-day absence adds the main question mark.

runners_data.name: Sir Garfield
runners_data.note: Back-to-back 6f wins on Good ground give him strong profile for today's conditions, and Jason Hart's booking is positive; he's a prominent racer who will benefit if the front three burn each other out, leaving him to sweep through late off a solid recent spin 16 days ago.
runners_data.comment: Sir Garfield won back-to-back races three and four starts back and returns here in good heart just 16 days later, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour; the risk is that his two most recent efforts were a sixth and eighth, suggesting he may need to rediscover that earlier form.

runners_data.name: Angel Gabriel
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old is fresh from just 9 days ago and has early-speed that will drag him into the pace battle; his form figures of 21-483 show promise but his stamina record at 6f on similar going is limited (2 runs, no wins or places), and he may be vulnerable if the early gallop is too fierce.
runners_data.comment: Angel Gabriel shaped well enough for a bold show, third last time out and a winner four starts back, and he arrives on the back of a quick nine-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going; the chief concern is that weight of 136 lb from stall one.

runners_data.name: Kolkata Knight
runners_data.note: Another confirmed front-runner, this three-year-old has been running mainly over 5f and now faces 6f — the extra furlong could find him out once the pace war takes hold; Tom Dascombe's record at 1/13 T14 is quiet, and his recent form figures (20840) include several poor runs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts but Kolkata Knight catches the eye on overall profile, having run over today's trip and going before; fourth two starts back shows he retains ability, and at 136 lb from stall six, the 15-day turnaround leaves him fresh and ready.

runners_data.name: On Edge
runners_data.note: Veteran of eight, wearing visor, and a genuine multiple winner on Good ground; he'll be prominent but not a true front-runner, which could allow him to sit just off the contested pace and produce a measured late challenge — his 1/5 T14 trainer stat is modest but his course-proven profile suits today.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of eight on our figures, On Edge is hard to fancy at these weights carrying 135 lb, though he does bring winning form in recent starts — a winner two starts back — and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Stellar Vision
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse on a 83-day break, with Pat Cosgrave in the saddle; his form shows a recent win over 7f on Soft and a pair of placed efforts on Good, and dropping back to 6f is a question, but the fast-run race should set things up perfectly for a late swoop if he can travel smoothly early.
runners_data.comment: Stellar Vision has been out of the placings in his last two starts, though a win four starts back and third-place finishes five and three starts back show he can perform at this level; the 83-day absence and a competitive 134 lb are the key questions here.

runners_data.name: Modern Times
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a recent win at 6f on Soft and multiple places on Good; James Owen's yard is busy at 9/45 T14, and Modern Times wearing a tongue-piece (tp) should help concentration — his ability to race off a strong pace without overreaching makes him a sneaky factor.
runners_data.comment: Comes here in fine heart after winning last time out, though a sixth three starts back and fifth four starts back show inconsistency; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 133 lb from stall three, and an official mark of 73 leaves something to prove against stronger.

runners_data.name: Sandscreendeliverd
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with solid placed form at 5f on Good ground, stepping up in trip to 6f for the first time; Charles Bishop takes the ride for a yard with minimal recent activity (0/1 T14), and the trip extension is unproven, though the strong gallop ahead of him should create the gaps he needs late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Sandscreendeliverd is hard to fancy despite finishing third in each of his last two outings; he has run over today's distance and going before, and 20 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Ruby's Profit, Kolkata Knight, and Angel Gabriel are all confirmed front-runners, guaranteeing a hot, contested pace from the off over Epsom's straight 6f on Good to Firm ground. These three will fight for the rail and the early advantage, meaning no single horse will dictate comfortably — instead, they will push each other through the first two furlongs at a searching gallop that tests stamina to the line. Sir Garfield and On Edge, both prominent types, will be drawn into a fast-run race whether they like it or not, sitting just off a pace that is effectively self-destructing. This shape strongly favours hold-up and late-running profiles — Stellar Vision and Sandscreendeliverd — as well as any prominent horse nimble enough to find cover early and sprint past a tiring lead pack in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out through the first half, leaving the hold-up horses to pick up the pieces late.
scenarios.body: Ruby's Profit, Kolkata Knight, and Angel Gabriel battle furiously for supremacy through the early stages, setting a pace that will unwind their finishing reserves on Good to Firm ground; Stellar Vision and Sandscreendeliverd, having been tucked in behind the carnage, are ideally placed to sprint through weakening rivals in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three pace horses establishes a clear lead by the two-furlong pole while the rivals burn each other out fighting for second.
scenarios.body: Rather than a three-way scrap dissolving into chaos, one runner — most likely Ruby's Profit with course experience over sprint trips or Angel Gabriel fresh from a win — finds a clean lead and dictates the terms, conserving enough energy to hold off challengers; the prominent types Sir Garfield and On Edge, sitting just off the pace, are best positioned to pounce if the leader ties up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce early but not quite suicidal, allowing a well-positioned prominent horse to swoop between the two-furlong and one-furlong marks before the hold-up horses can close.
scenarios.body: Sir Garfield, who has won twice recently at 6f on Good ground, and On Edge, a consistent front-up type, could slot into second or third gear early and produce a well-timed run through the final furlong without overexerting themselves chasing the leaders; Modern Times, dropping back in trip from 7f, would also appreciate a pace that doesn't burn the race off immediately.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Soft Pace, Front Runner Holds
scenarios.trigger: If the three nominally front-running horses fail to push hard against each other and a falsely slow pace develops, allowing one to lob along and hold on.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires at least two of Ruby's Profit, Kolkata Knight, or Angel Gabriel to concede the lead without a battle — unlikely given all three have strong early-speed profiles — but if it happens, the hold-up horses Stellar Vision and Sandscreendeliverd would be caught flat-footed finishing from too far back with insufficient pace to reel in a fresh leader.

watchPoints.text: Ruby's Profit, Kolkata Knight, and Angel Gabriel are all confirmed front-runners — watch the first furlong closely for a pace war that could dramatically compromise all three, making their final-furlong stamina the decisive factor.

Stellar Vision returns from 83 days off and is a hold-up horse switching from 7f to 6f — if he fails to travel smoothly in the first half, Pat Cosgrave may not have enough track left to deliver his challenge.

Sir Garfield's back-to-back wins at today's trip and going make him the most course-and-distance proven runner; watch whether Jason Hart can slot him into a prominent position without getting burned by the pace battle ahead.
Sandscreendeliverd is unproven over 6f, having run exclusively at 5f; the extra furlong in a fast-run race is a genuine stamina question that Charles Bishop will need to manage carefully.
Modern Times has been in consistent form including a recent win, but his trainer James Owen's T14 return of 9/45 suggests the yard is firing in numbers — check for market moves as a sign of intent.

races.name: Betfred 'Play Fred's £5 Million' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mrembo
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with winning form at 1m2f on Good ground; Portman's seven-year-old is well-handicapped off OR 58 and thrives when allowed to bowl along uncontested — the Epsom straight sets her up perfectly from the front.
runners_data.comment: Mrembo has run over today's trip and going before and steps up from an official mark of 58 carrying 138 lb from stall four, with our rating suggesting she holds solid claims at this level; the concern is that in her last six starts she has managed only one win, making a return to that form the key question.

runners_data.name: Gretna Dreams
runners_data.note: True hold-up type from Stuart Williams's yard who has placed on good ground at this trip; Pat Cosgrave will need a stronger gallop than this pace map suggests to deliver her late challenge, and the slow early fractions are a concern.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and winless in her last five starts, Gretna Dreams nonetheless heads the ratings here and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making her the one to side with from stall two off 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Offiah's Boy
runners_data.note: Has winning and placed form on Firm and Good ground and is a natural closer by style, though the surplus of hold-up horses in this field means he may push forward earlier than his ideal — his STYLE_FIT score of 0.94 signals he is racing partially out of role.
runners_data.comment: Offiah's Boy won last time out and is quickly back ten days later, bringing strong recent momentum and experience of today's trip and conditions; however, his form in the last six starts shows inconsistency, and he carries 137 lb from stall three.

runners_data.name: Haveagobeau
runners_data.note: Olivia Haines claims 7lbs on a horse with solid form at 1m-1m2f on Good ground, and his recent win at this trip makes him a genuine contender if he can access a prominent position; the claim helps offset the weight.
runners_data.comment: Haveagobeau won last time out and was second two starts back, but fifth on three and four starts back tempers confidence; he has run over today's trip and going, carries 134 lb from stall 10, and comes here on a sharp 20-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Celtic Spirit
runners_data.note: Karen Jewell's four-year-old has placed twice at 1m2f on Good ground and is a natural hold-up horse pushed forward by the crowded closer contingent; the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 tempers confidence, but the good-going profile is genuinely suitable.
runners_data.comment: Celtic Spirit has finished second twice in his last five starts and has already run over today's distance and going, with our rating of 60 suggesting he merits respect; the chief concern is that he remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Pangbourne
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's three-year-old returns from a 95-day break and has placed twice at 1m2f on Standard, with only one run on Good — freshness and the absence of a recent race is a notable flag, though the 3lb claimer for Ashley Lewis helps.
runners_data.comment: Pangbourne's back-to-back runner-up finishes three and four starts back show she can get competitive, and having run over today's trip and going counts in her favour, but 95 days off the track is the obvious concern for a filly yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Time To Sparkle
runners_data.note: The only confirmed prominent-type outside the leader, Alice Bond's 5lb claim is a bonus and the horse's three consecutive thirds at 1m-1m2f on Good ground underline course-going suitability; the natural position second to the leader is ideal in this shape.

runners_data.name: All About George
runners_data.note: Josephine Gordon partners a horse whose last five runs at 1m-1m2f on Good and Firm show no win; he is a genuine hold-up horse shown in midfield by redistribution alone, and the STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 reflects genuine tactical compromise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, All About George is hard to fancy despite the experience over today's trip and going; drawing stall one and returning after a sharp 14-day break are the few neutral angles here.

runners_data.name: Lady Margret
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Lady Margret has shown little to inspire confidence from draw 11 carrying 126 lb, and while she has run over today's distance and going before, her recent string of modest finishes makes her hard to fancy at the foot of the ratings.

runners_data.name: Private Project
runners_data.note: Pat Phelan's three-year-old has placed at 1m2f on Good ground and shows some promise, but the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 confirms he will be racing away from his natural position; a light weight of 9st 6lbs via Egan is the most tangible angle.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in recent starts, Private Project nevertheless brings placed form to the table — third last time out and a third four starts back — and she returns fit on 13 days' rest having already experienced today's trip and conditions, though her official mark of 48 suggests she faces a stiff task from stall 7.

runners_data.name: Cormorant Rock
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's second runner in the race — note the 0/15 T14 strike rate — is a natural hold-up horse with five straight runs at 1m-1m2f on Good ground but no win from any of them; the STYLE_FIT of 0.92 and the trainer's form dip limit confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Cormorant Rock has shown little to suggest he can turn things around here, ranked eighth of ten on our figures, and his fourth-place finishes represent the best of a modest recent sequence; some experience over today's trip and going and a quick turnaround of 13 days are slim consolations.

races.paceDynamic: Mrembo is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 11-runner field over 1m2f at Epsom on Good to Firm ground, and with no natural rival to push her along, Hector Crouch can dictate a controlled, measured gallop from the off — she has winning form at this trip on similar going and is firmly in her element. Time To Sparkle is the only genuine prominent-type likely to sit in her slipstream, meaning the early pace will be steady rather than searching, compressing the race into a stamina-test with a premium on a strong Epsom-style finish. The field carries a surplus of hold-up horses — Celtic Spirit, Offiah's Boy, Private Project, All About George, Lady Margret and Cormorant Rock are all true closers redistributed into the midfield positions because there simply is not enough genuine pace ahead of them; of those, Celtic Spirit and Offiah's Boy are most likely to push forward and secure a better position than their natural style suggests. A steady pace with one horse in total control overwhelmingly favours horses who can travel prominently, switch off, and quicken from a good position in the straight — sit-and-sprint types will be dangerous; pure deep closers will face a wall of stopping horses ahead of them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mrembo Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Mrembo secures the lead without contest and Crouch dictates a comfortable tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Mrembo controls every fraction on a track that rewards front-runners who can quicken into Epsom's punishing straight, and a steady gallop plays to the stamina of prominent horses who save ground. Time To Sparkle, sitting second throughout, is ideally placed to pounce without burning petrol chasing a fast early pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace bunches the field and a prominent or midfield horse tracks Mrembo to take over in the home straight.
scenarios.body: A compressed, slow-run race turns the finish into a sprint, and horses who travel near the head of affairs without expending energy early hold a decisive positional advantage on this track. Time To Sparkle and Haveagobeau both have winning form at similar trips on good ground and the tactical experience to exploit this.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Lifts Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If Celtic Spirit or Offiah's Boy push forward from their redistributed positions and inject a more genuine gallop into the middle section.
scenarios.body: A more honest tempo stretches the field and rewards horses with genuine stamina reserves; those who have settled mid-pack while the pace was compressed can challenge with a sustained run rather than a sprint. Gretna Dreams, a natural hold-up type with good-going form, and Pangbourne, who ran well on similar ground when fresh, could each emerge if the tempo finally brings closing form into play.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely deceptive and the hold-up contingent gets a strong enough gallop to bring them home late.
scenarios.body: This outcome depends on redistributed hold-up horses — Offiah's Boy, All About George, Private Project — actually racing out of their natural role or receiving unexpected assistance from a genuine tempo, making it structurally the least likely scenario. Gretna Dreams is the most credible closer here given she is a true hold-up type who has hit the frame on good ground at this trip, but even she needs a significantly faster gallop than this race shape suggests.

watchPoints.text: Mrembo — if Hector Crouch gets a completely uncontested lead by the time the field turns into Epsom's home straight, she has the form and the fitness to prove very hard to peg back at a winnable mark of OR 58.

Time To Sparkle — the only other runner with a naturally prominent style; watch whether Alice Bond positions her immediately behind Mrembo in the first furlong, as the horse is 0W from 9 attempts and needs the setup to go exactly right.

Celtic Spirit and Offiah's Boy — both are hold-up horses flagged REDISTRIBUTED who may try to push forward early; if either gains a prominent berth unexpectedly, monitor whether the pace lifts and stretches the field in a way that changes the race shape.

Pangbourne — 95 days off the track is the longest absence in the field; watch the market move at the off and pay close attention to his early body language as a first-time-in-a-while runner in a race where getting position early matters.

Haveagobeau's claim angle — Olivia Haines's 7lb allowance is the biggest claim in the field and could be decisive in a tight finish; watch whether the pairing gets into a prominent position or is forced to make ground from the rear.

races.name: Betfred 'Double Delight' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Chantelle
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's filly returns just 15 days after her last run in excellent form (1-122), and her prominent-racing style positions her perfectly to track a hot pace without being embroiled in it; two recent wins on Soft at 7f raise a mild stamina question over 1m½f on faster ground, but her Good going record (sim-going: 1 win from 4) shows she handles the surface.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent and in form, Chantelle has won twice in her last four starts and was runner-up on both most recent outings, arriving here just 15 days on from that effort with experience of today's trip and going; the weight of 134 lb is the principal concern.

runners_data.name: Loblolly
runners_data.note: David Probert rides a consistent but win-shy sort (form: -63347) whose trainer Woods has no wins from 6 in the last 14 days, dampening confidence; earns credit for placing three times at 8f-10f on Good, and the longer trip here may suit better than her sprint outings — but her front-running style means she must absorb the pace battle rather than avoid it, and her headgear (p) suggests she needs keeping up to her work.|
runners_data.comment: Loblolly has shown a consistent level with two thirds in recent starts, and he has run over today's trip and going, making him a lively danger at 132 lb; the risk is that he has been winless in his last five starts and must find improvement to go one better.

runners_data.name: Trio
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's yard is in form (7/43 over 14 days) and this filly arrives on the back of back-to-back wins at 8f on Good — the strongest recent profile in the race; she is a confirmed front-runner who must battle Loblolly and Mystic Moment for early supremacy, and while her class edges the rivals, she needs to emerge from that three-way duel with enough left for the 1m½f distance she is tackling for the first time.|
runners_data.comment: Trio arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and with experience of today's trip and conditions, making her a serious threat here; the main risk is that she meets the top-rated runner off 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Mystic Moment
runners_data.note: Neil Mulholland's runner is 44 days off the track — the longest break in the field — and a cold trainer stat (0/5 over 14 days) dims expectations significantly; her form reads poorly (37-658) and she has struggled at 7f-8f on Good, suggesting the step to 1m½f is speculative rather than logical; as a front-runner she adds to the pace pressure but looks the least likely of the trio to survive it all the way to the line.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Mystic Moment does at least bring distance and going experience to this, and a rating of 91 puts her clear of her three rivals on our figures, though her recent string of mid-field finishes demands more here.

races.paceDynamic: Trio, Loblolly, and Mystic Moment are all confirmed front-runners in a field of just four, guaranteeing an aggressive pace battle from the outset over this 1m½f trip at Epsom on Good to Firm ground. One of the three will likely assume control, but the internal friction between them will ensure fractions are brisk and the race is run as a genuine stamina test rather than a tactical affair. Chantelle, the sole prominent-style runner, sits ideally placed to track the pace war from just off the leaders without expending early energy in the fight for position. This race shape emphatically favours a horse with prominent-to-tracking ability and proven stamina reserves — specifically, a runner who can sit close enough to capitalise when the pace-setters tie each other up in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out in an honest gallop and the race turns into a stamina test from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Trio, Loblolly, and Mystic Moment trade fractions hard from the outset, leaving the one who can sustain longest at risk of being collared late; Chantelle, travelling just off the battle, pounces as the pace-setters empty inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Controls
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner establishes clean early supremacy and the others settle or drop away, allowing a dominant lead.
scenarios.body: Trio, whose recent back-to-back wins at 8f on Good suggest genuine improvement, gets first run out of the stalls and dictates at a controlled tempo; without a true battle to drain reserves, they grind out the finish and hold on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Attrition, Survivor Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel is so fierce that all three leaders flatten out simultaneously and the race becomes a gruelling battle of who stops last.
scenarios.body: The Good to Firm ground keeps times honest and none of the three leaders can find another gear from two furlongs out; whichever of Trio or Loblolly has the deepest reserves scrambles home as the others weaken.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset, Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If an unusually slow or muddling early pace develops and the race becomes a sprint finish from the home straight.
scenarios.body: With no true hold-up runner to produce a sustained late run, a compressed finish with minimal gaps suits whichever front-runner is freshest; Mystic Moment, the least exposed at pace, could steal an advantage if rivals are caught flat-footed.

watchPoints.text: Trio v Loblolly v Mystic Moment — watch which of the three front-runners actually clears first at the start; whoever gets the cleanest break controls the tempo and avoids the worst of the pace friction.

Mystic Moment's 44-day absence is a significant unknown — watch her in the paddock and at the start for signs of rustiness that could cause her to drop away early and compromise the anticipated pace scenario.

Chantelle's connections (Prescott) are renowned for placing horses precisely — watch her market move; if she shortens significantly she may be better suited to this longer trip than her Soft-ground wins suggest.
The step to 1m½f is untested for Trio — if she shows any sign of idling or shortening stride from two furlongs out, Chantelle has the position to pounce immediately.

Loblolly's headgear (p — presumably a hood or similar) is worth noting at the start; if it is removed or having a first-time effect it could alter how she jumps and whether she leads or sits just off Trio early.|

races.name: Betfred 'Follow Us On X' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: A La Noche
runners_data.note: Long-absent hold-up horse (1,059 days off) returning for Oliver Cole; recent form came on soft ground and the step up to good-to-firm over 7f at Epsom represents a significant unknown, making her hard to assess on current evidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and returning from a layoff of nearly three years, A La Noche faces a stern fitness test, though he has run over today's trip before and our rating marks him as the top-rated runner in the field.

runners_data.name: Red Mirage
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type who has placed on good ground over 7f before; Jason Hart partners an eight-year-old who knows his job from a handy position, and a return to Epsom on a quick surface suits his travelling style.

runners_data.name: King Of War
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who landed a 7f handicap on good ground and has strong course-type form at this trip; J F Egan has ridden him recently, tongue-tie applied, and an uncontested lead on good-to-firm could see him control this from pillar to post.
runners_data.comment: King Of War won one of his last five starts and shapes with some each-way claims after finishing third two starts back, though an unplaced effort latest gives pause; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 141 lb from stall four is the challenge to overcome.

runners_data.name: Freddie's Star
runners_data.note: Prominent racer stepping back to 7f from an 8f base, wearing a hood; Roger Teal's yard is in modest form (T14: 1/10) and the horse has not placed in nine recent attempts on good ground, which limits confidence despite a handy racing position.
runners_data.comment: Freddie's Star has run over today's distance and going before, and a fourth last time out — his best recent effort — suggests he is building form from stall two off 31 days, with our rating of 71 marking him a genuine threat; the concern is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Ararat
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who has shown placed form over 7f on good ground; David Probert rides for the Rachel Cook & John Bridger yard, and his run 11 days ago keeps him fit, though he has yet to win in 15 similar-going starts.
runners_data.comment: Ararat has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 75 puts him among the strongest in this field — but he is winless in his last six starts, which is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Play Me
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent-to-midfield type with two wins on good ground and a win over this course-type trip; Donagh Murphy (7) claims 7lbs, Jim Boyle's horse is race-fit after a run nine days ago, and his good-going stats (12 runs, 2W, 6P) make him interesting in the right shape.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way back in ninth last time out, Play Me faces a stiff task ranked only seventh of nine on our figures, and his recent record shows just one win in his last six starts; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a return to form cannot be entirely ruled out.

runners_data.name: Eyes Front
runners_data.note: Won last time over 7f on good ground and is equipped with a hood; Alistair Rawlinson rides the three-year-old whose hold-up style has adapted to tracking from off the pace — strong recent form gives him claims if the prominent pace sets up a late challenge.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of nine on our figures and a winner only once in his last six starts, Eyes Front faces a stiff ask here, though he does return on a quick turnaround of 15 days following that recent victory, and has experience of today's trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Spacewoman
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's three-year-old is a natural hold-up filly — her true style is to close from the rear — but with the field holding several genuine closers, she is mapped to midfield rather than her preferred position; on going and form she has shown, she handles fast conditions well enough but racing out of role tempers expectation.
runners_data.comment: Spacewoman won three starts back and was third two starts back, so there is recent encouragement, though a fifth last time out tempers enthusiasm; she has run over today's trip and going, carries 131 lb from stall 3, and our rating edges above her official mark.

runners_data.name: Ice Cube
runners_data.note: Won last time over 7f on good ground and Charles Bishop has strong stats for Richard Spencer; the horse wears a hood and is a genuine hold-up type by inclination, though the field shape means he cannot drop out naturally — he is finishing from a position that isn't truly his own, and that structural displacement reduces the value of his recent win as a guide here.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Ice Cube faces a stiff task, having finished fifth or sixth in four of his last six starts; his recent win is a plus, however, as is experience of today's distance and going, and he arrives here 29 days fresh.

races.paceDynamic: King Of War is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, he should stride clear from the gates and control an honest but manageable gallop over Epsom's flat 7f on good-to-firm ground. Red Mirage and Freddie's Star are the likeliest horses to press from prominent positions, but neither is a natural tearaway, so the tempo should be regulated rather than frantic. The field carries more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Spacewoman and Ice Cube are true closers displaced into midfield, meaning they are effectively racing out of their natural role and their chance in a shape that requires a late surge from behind the field is structurally discounted. With one uncontested pace-setter dictating a measured gallop on fast ground at Epsom, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off King Of War and pounce in the straight, rather than genuine hold-up horses who need a stronger pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: King Of War Controls
scenarios.trigger: If King Of War leads unchallenged and the pace is honest but measured, setting up a straight fight from the front.
scenarios.body: King Of War dictates every yard at a sensible clip on good-to-firm ground, and his rivals track him without ever seriously threatening until the Epsom straight; horses close to the pace who can quicken from a position of control benefit most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Red Mirage or Freddie's Star track King Of War closely and sprint past him inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A controlled pace allows the prominent trackers to travel sweetly in behind the leader before unleashing a finish on ground that rewards those who have conserved energy; Eyes Front, winner last time, is ideally placed to join this move from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If King Of War sets a stronger gallop than expected and the pace proves genuinely taxing enough to bring the midfield into play.
scenarios.body: A faster tempo stretches the field and those sitting in mid-division — Play Me and Ararat — get the strong pace they need to make sustained late progress; both have shown ability to finish well on similar ground and trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Ups Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and Spacewoman or Ice Cube, despite racing out of their natural hold-up role, find room to finish through.
scenarios.body: Both horses are racing structurally out of position and the going is quick enough to blunt their trademark late kick; this scenario requires both an unusually strong gallop and clear late running, making it the least likely shape in this field configuration.

watchPoints.text: Watch King Of War's behaviour in the early furlongs — if J F Egan is forced to use him up to repel any unexpected early pressure from Red Mirage or Freddie's Star, his stamina for the Epsom straight could be compromised and the race opens up considerably.

Monitor Play Me in the betting; two wins on good ground, a 7lb claim from Donagh Murphy, and a race-fit run nine days ago make him a live contender if the pace quickens sufficiently to bring the midfield into the race in the final two furlongs.

Spacewoman and Ice Cube are both racing out of their natural hold-up roles due to field congestion at the rear — if punters back them on the strength of recent form without accounting for the positional disadvantage, their market positions may overstate their winning chance in this specific race shape.

Eyes Front is the horse most likely to bridge the gap between the prominent group and the midfield; his recent win over 7f on good ground and adaptable style mean he could be dangerous if King Of War's gallop is strong enough to string the field out early.
